mt: 'OLMOTRACE' ON THE OVERVIEW — THE TRACING SYSTEM AT ITS GRAIN, ITS MECHANISM FROM THE BLOG; A VERBATIM MATCH GIVEN AS 'THE EXACT TRAINING TEXT THAT INFLUENCED' A RESPONSE; WHAT A MATCHED DOCUMENT IS SHOWN UNDER NOT REACHED
d: THE TOOL, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'OLMoTrace is the first real-time system that traces language model outputs back to multi-trillion-token training datasets. Developed by the Allen Institute for AI (Ai2) and winner of Best Demo at ACL 2025, it lets users inspect the exact training text that influenced a model's response.' How it works (verbatim matching, the infini-gram index, filtering by unigram probability and ranking by BM25, the three supported OLMo models); four use cases (fact-checking, hallucination diagnosis, creative tracing, arithmetic and memory analysis); pointers to the blog post and the arXiv listing; an embedded Ai2 video (2:17); an offer on the GitHub code or infini-gram indexing. Six cards: Ai2, arXiv, ACL Anthology (two), Hugging Face, YouTube.
reading: The innocent reading first. Asked for the tool by name, the Overview says what it is, who made it, how it finds and ranks matches, which models it serves and what it is for, from Ai2's blog, the paper and its listings.
findings: THE MECHANISM AT ITS GRAIN. 'It tokenizes the model's generated text and scans for maximal matching word spans', 'Spans are filtered by unigram probability and mapped to top context documents ranked by BM25 relevance', and the three models 'OLMo 2 32B Instruct, OLMo 2 13B Instruct, and OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct'. The blog: 'Maximality : The span is not a subspan of another span that meets the above two criteria.', 'keeps the K spans with the smallest unigram probability', 'in the document panel we rank all documents by a BM25 score in descending order.' The 'extended infini-gram suffix array index' agrees with the abstract ('Powered by an extended version of infini-gram (Liu et al., 2024)'). The corpus is given as 'multi-trillion-token'; the blog's count for the 32B model, 'about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens', and its cap of 'up to 10 document snippets' per span are not carried.

THE MATCH GIVEN AS INFLUENCE. 'it lets users inspect the exact training text that influenced a model's response.' Ai2's own terms are hedged: 'inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences', 'the model could have easily learned it through memorization', 'The interpretation of text matches with training data is quite nuanced.' The census row reads a highlight as a witness that a stretch of output has a verbatim antecedent, the evidence for #1543's S = retrieved, and records that 'Verbatim matching is not causal influence'. 'Creative Tracing: Identify where distinctive phrases, styles, or patterns originated across training corpora' carries the blog's 'trace certain LM-generated expressions back to the training documents' out to styles and patterns, which leave no verbatim span to highlight; the abstract's bound is 'verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora'.

THE VERIFICATION MOVED. 'Fact-Checking: Verify whether a model's statement is grounded in authentic training data or synthesized from noise.' The blog puts the check with the user: 'If you personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources, you can gain confidence that this piece of information generated by the model is factually correct.' In the composition the match does the verifying; the blog's 'low relevance' label for spans whose documents are less relevant is not carried.

THE PRIZE AND THE SPEED FROM THE CARDS. 'winner of Best Demo at ACL 2025' is on the first ACL Anthology card ('System: OLMoTrace (Best Demo, ACL 2025)'); the arXiv page the census saved has 'ACL 2025 demo track'. The second ACL card gives 'within 4.5 seconds', the abstract 'within a few seconds'. The blog's date, 'April 9, 2025', and its signature, 'Jiacheng Liu et al.', are not in the composition, which names no person.

WHAT A DOCUMENT IS SHOWN UNDER NOT REACHED. The census row: the saved sources do not say whether the side panel shows 'a document's author, title or source address'. The composition speaks of 'top context documents' and 'training documents' and says nothing of what a matched document carries; the census row's further bound, that productive transformation (#1543's W) leaves no verbatim span, is the limit the composition's 'styles, or patterns' passes over.
analysis: The tool composed accurately at the level of its mechanism, from its own blog and paper. A verbatim match becomes 'the exact training text that influenced' a response, the user's verification becomes the match's, and creative tracing widens from expressions to styles; what a matched document is shown under is not reached.

atomset.name: OLMoTrace
atomset.type_basis: A tool: its maker's blog and its paper's arXiv page, saved 2026-11-01, describe it as a feature in the Ai2 Playground that traces the outputs of language models back to their full training data in real time. Read on the site template.

evidence.record_quote: Today we introduce OLMoTrace, a one-of-a-kind feature in the Ai2 Playground that lets you trace the outputs of language models back to their full, multi-trillion-token training data in real time.
OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.

atoms.reference: Ai2 (The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence), as a feature of the Ai2 Playground; the blog signed 'Jiacheng Liu et al.', the paper by Jiacheng Liu and 30 others.

evidence.record_quote: © The Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence - All Rights Reserved.
by Jiacheng Liu and 30 other authors

atoms.reference: Introduced 9 April 2025 (the blog; arXiv v1 the same day); the paper in the ACL 2025 demo track.
Verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora: long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the model's training data.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace finds and shows verbatim matches between segments of language model output and documents in the training text corpora.
The highlights indicate long and unique spans that appear verbatim at least once in the training data of this model.

atoms.reference: The full training data of Ai2's three flagship models (OLMo 2 32B Instruct, OLMo 2 13B Instruct, OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct), for the 32B model five datasets of about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens; applicable to any model whose training data is accessible.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace is available today with our three flagship models: OLMo 2 32B Instruct , OLMo 2 13B Instruct , and OLMoE 1B 7B Instruct , and it can be applied to any language model for which you have access to the training data.
In total, these five datasets contain about 3.2 billion documents and 4.6 trillion tokens, and OLMoTrace matches against all of them.

atoms.reference: To enable researchers, developers and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences; shown for fact checking, hallucination and creativity.

evidence.record_quote: We developed OLMoTrace to enable researchers, developers, and the general public to inspect where and how language models may have learned to generate certain word sequences.
We showcase how it can be used to explore fact checking, hallucination, and the creativity of language models.

atoms.reference: Publicly available and fully open-source, its source code released; the interpretation of matches called 'quite nuanced', and factual confidence left to the user's own verification of the documents' sources.

evidence.record_quote: OLMoTrace is publicly available and fully open-source.
We also release our source code .
The interpretation of text matches with training data is quite nuanced.
If you personally verify that these documents come from trusted sources, you can gain confidence that this piece of information generated by the model is factually correct.

atoms.reference: Built on infini-gram, with which the training data is indexed.

evidence.record_quote: To speed up computation, we index the training data with infini-gram and develop a novel parallel algorithm, reducing the time complexity of span finding from the naive O(L^2 * N) to O(L * log N)
